                    ### Question
                    A 21-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 2-week history of progressive shortness of breath and intermittent cough with blood-tinged sputum. During this time, he has also noticed blood in his urine. He has no history of serious illness and does not take any medications. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 92/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 152/90 mm Hg. Cardiopulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Urinalysis is positive for blood and results of a direct enzyme-linked immunoassay are positive for anti-GBM antibodies. The pathogenesis of this patient's disease is most similar to which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Henoch-Schönlein purpura
opb. Polyarteritis nodosa
opc. Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
opd. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
ope. Graft versus host disease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's positive anti-GBM antibodies indicate Goodpasture syndrome, which is characterized by simultaneous lung and kidney involvement, leading to symptoms such as hemoptysis and hematuria. This pathogenesis is distinct from Henoch-Schönlein purpura, which primarily involves skin and gastrointestinal symptoms, and is not characterized by anti-GBM antibodies. While poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis involves glomerular damage, it does not typically present with pulmonary symptoms or anti-GBM antibodies. Polyarteritis nodosa can involve renal symptoms but lacks the specific anti-GBM antibody association and pulmonary hemorrhage seen in Goodpasture syndrome. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia and graft versus host disease do not align with the specific renal and pulmonary manifestations of this case. Therefore, the most similar pathogenesis to this patient's condition is Goodpasture syndrome, which is not listed among the options but is closest to the autoimmune processes described in the options. The evidence paths confirm the lung and kidney involvement associated with anti-GBM disease, reinforcing the diagnosis of Goodpasture syndrome.
